The Dragoon holds its sword high on the right: the proper warrior's stance. Before it, the old man brings his short sword to middle guard, ready for that heavy blade.

A short sword receives first and attacks afterward. That is its basic arrangement. With such limited reach, first attack, then regret is not a useful alternative.

But the old man is deliberately violating the arrangement. The point is a little low. The weight is too far forward. For receiving a blow, this posture is making every possible inconvenience.

Plainly, he does not intend to receive. He intends to attack.

Against a long sword that owns the distance, this is recklessness with the madness already inside. Yes, a short-sword master can steal that distance. But feints are needed, some bargaining with the opponent's intentions. You cannot simply walk in and announce that the range now belongs to you.

Then what hidden plan has this old man brought?

—Nothing.

Not emptiness of mind. Foolishness of mind. There is a difference, bhai.

　――何もない。

　無の境地……否。
　愚の境地であった。

The Dragoon before him has one foolish obsession packed into its chest: smash whatever is standing there. Against that, some clever little parry here, some neat little deflection there—will these win?

Nahin.

That towering conviction will crush such cleverness without even making a separate effort for it.

Wisdom can defeat folly. True. But cheap cleverness is not wisdom merely because it has come wearing wisdom's spectacles.

One road remains. Become a fool also. Meet it there.

The old man has his own foolishness: this man must be stopped by him. Nobody else will do.

He can run. He can leave it to somebody. Who will blame him? Nobody.

But he has chosen. The duty was free to put down; he has picked it up with both hands.

Why? One small attachment. A world from long ago, with only himself, this man, and one woman in it.

The woman is gone. Toh, the man who remains is his to settle with.

In that world there were three people. Bas. Three.

　まず最初は山から響いた轟音。

　激しい音ではあったが、それはただ、それだけだ。
　地上は大きく鳴動したかもしれないが、空にあって
は耳孔の鼓膜を震わせたに過ぎない。

　その直後、月山が姿を現した。
　しかも当人は、そのことにすぐには気付かなかった。

　……おかしい。
　轟音に驚いて術を解いてしまったというのなら――
風魔の頭領が音如きで？――自分で気付かぬ筈がない。
　驚いていなかったなら、術の解ける理由がない。

　理屈が合わぬ、この矛盾。
　ここだ。
　この裏に真相がある。

　だがそれは何だ!?
　あと、何か一つ――発想の取っ掛かりがあれば――

　まず最初は山から響いた轟音。

　激しい音ではあったが、それはただ、それだけだ。
　地上は大きく鳴動したかもしれないが、空にあって
は耳孔の鼓膜を震わせたに過ぎない。

　その直後、月山が姿を現した。
　しかも当人は、そのことにすぐには気付かなかった。

　……おかしい。
　轟音に驚いて術を解いてしまったというのなら――
風魔の頭領が音如きで？――自分で気付かぬ筈がない。
　驚いていなかったなら、術の解ける理由がない。

　理屈が合わぬ、この矛盾。
　ここだ。
　この裏に真相がある。

　だがそれは何だ!?
　あと、何か一つ――発想の取っ掛かりがあれば――

...Mil gaye! Beside the old shrine: two warriors. Mount Haguro and Mount Yudono!

Here was the whole secret of Mist-Hiding. These two sat hidden on the ground, casting the art on Gassan!

Now everything fitted. An unreasonable art? Of course. Two whole frames were supplying it. Probably one handled the optics, the other the signals. And Gassan's strange chanting was not an incantation at all. He was signaling these fellows!

Their only work: maintain the art. His only work: fight. Toh naturally it lasted so long. We had been wondering how one man was carrying the cupboard. Two more were holding it from behind.

Three frames making one invincible warrior. Like the Three Mountains of Dewa making one faith.

Then the shock—presumably the magistrate and Elder Yagenta clashing—disturbed the casters' concentration. Mist-Hiding broke. By sheer chance, we were handed that opening. Without it, this three-in-one arrangement would probably have finished us.

　この二者が妖術・霧隠の正体。
　地上に姿を隠し、<ruby>月山に陰義を掛けていた<rt>・・・・・・・・・・・</rt></ruby>術師！

　月山の怪詠唱は陰義の<ruby>呪句<rt>コマンド</rt></ruby>に非ず、二人への合図！

　二騎が陰義の行使に専念し、月山が戦闘のみを担当
していたのであれば、術の異様な長時間維持とて何の
不思議もない。

　彼らは三騎で一騎の無敵者を成していたのだ。
　あたかも、出羽三山が一つの信仰を成すように！

　代官と弥源太老の激突によるものだろう衝撃が術者
の集中を乱し、霧隠の術を解かせるという偶然の配剤
がもしも、なかったなら――
　おそらくこの三位一体を破るには至らなかったろう。
